facts.text: The hotel is directly opposite Kensington Palace, with views across the gardens to the palace.

facts.text: Cheneston's restaurant serves modern British cuisine.

facts.text: Traditional British afternoon tea is served in The Park Lounge.

facts.excerpt: Rich dark wood panelling, sophisticated leather and tartan furnishings, and sporting artwork by renowned Belgian artist Elie Lambert

facts.excerpt: The resistance pool, cold plunge and infrared sauna provide a restorative setting to unwind and rebalance at your own pace.

facts.text: No two rooms or suites are alike; rooms are decorated with fine fabrics, fresh flowers, antique furnishings and rare artworks.

facts.text: The Hermes Suite is a Grand Master Suite with a four-poster bed and a collection of Hermes scarves.

facts.text: The Noel Coward Suite has art deco touches and antiques.
facts.excerpt: The Noel Coward Suite, with its art deco touches and antiques

facts.text: The Kensington Garden Suite is a split-level Master Suite with floor-to-ceiling bay windows.
facts.excerpt: Floor-to-ceiling bay windows span this unique split level Master Suite.

facts.text: Suite guests can book in-room private performances by a Royal Philharmonic Orchestra solo harpist or a string trio.
facts.excerpt: Watch and listen as one of the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra's wonderful solo harpists or a talented string trio plays a selection of your favourite songs

facts.text: The Residences have two or three bedrooms, fully equipped kitchens and private access via their own front door.
facts.excerpt: With elegant two and three bedroom Residences, families can enjoy a refined London base with separate lounges, fully equipped kitchens and dining areas for family-style meals, plus the freedom of private access via your own front door.

facts.text: Children under 12 get complimentary breakfast.

facts.text: Family touches on request include a kids' teddy bear turndown.
